results.content: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has announced that outstanding promotion arrears for staff promoted in 2025 are expected to be paid on November 16, 2026.

results.title: IERPP demands account of $4bn 24-Hour Economy before rollout of $10bn New Economy
results.content: The Institute of Economic Research and Public Policy (IERPP) has challenged the Mahama administration to account for the financing, projects and jobs associated with its $4 billion 24-Hour Economy programme before proceeding with the proposed $10 billion New Economy initiative. The institute’s Executive Director, Professor Isaac Boadi, says the government must provide verifiable evidence of the original programme’s performance, including funds disbursed, projects implemented and employment created. Speaking at a press conference at the IERPP Conference Room in Adabraka, Accra, on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, he questioned the credibility of announcing a substantially larger economic initiative without first publishing a comprehensive account of the existing programme.

results.title: African climate lead demands action for local communities at Liberia summit
results.content: At a strategic gathering of climate negotiators and national focal points, the African Group of Negotiators (AGN) issued a direct call to prioritize local implementation over international diplomacy alone, warning that global agreements mean little if they do not empower everyday citizens.

results.title: Adu-Boahene trial must be decided on evidence, not public pressure – Group
results.content: A group has called for the protection of the judge presiding over the criminal trial of former National Signals Bureau director Kwabena Adu-Boahene and two others from political pressure and other forms of improper influence. The group, convened by Rev. DK Odei-Appiah, said Justice Francis Apangabuno Achibonga must be allowed to determine the case independently, without intimidation or public pressure to deliver a particular outcome. Speaking at a press conference at the Ghana International Press Centre in Accra on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, Rev. Odei-Appiah said the coalition’s intervention was intended to protect judicial independence, the presumption of innocence and public confidence in Ghana’s criminal justice system.

results.title: Adutwum calls for mandatory annual child protection training for school staff
results.content: Former Education Minister Dr Yaw Osei Adutwum has called for mandatory child protection training for teachers and other education workers at the beginning of every academic year as part of efforts to prevent sexual abuse in schools. He said the training should be compulsory for all school staff, with participants required to acknowledge that they have received instruction on child protection and understand the conduct expected of them. Speaking in an interview on JoyNews’ The Pulse, Dr Adutwum said the measure would help ensure that teachers understand their responsibilities towards students and the consequences of inappropriate conduct.

results.title: Adutwum wants sex offenders register to screen teachers and school workers
results.content: Former Education Minister Dr Yaw Osei Adutwum has called for mandatory fingerprint background checks as a condition for teacher licensing, arguing that stronger vetting is needed to prevent individuals with relevant criminal records from working in schools. He has also proposed establishing a sex offenders register that would be checked against the fingerprints of teachers and other education workers before they are allowed to work in public or private schools. Speaking in an interview on JoyNews’ The Pulse, Dr Adutwum questioned the effectiveness of existing background checks, claiming that the current teacher licensing process does not adequately establish whether applicants have criminal records.

results.title: Adutwum proposes criminal sanctions for teachers who fail to report child abuse
results.content: Former Education Minister Dr Yaw Osei Adutwum has called for mandatory reporting laws requiring teachers, medical professionals and other relevant professionals to report suspected child sexual abuse, with criminal sanctions for those who fail to do so. He argues that Ghana’s current system relies too heavily on the Ghana Education Service (GES) to handle abuse cases, making stronger legal obligations and enforcement necessary to protect students. Speaking in an interview on JoyNews’ The Pulse, Dr Adutwum said reporting suspected abuse should be a legal duty rather than a matter of personal discretion. “As a medical doctor who gets wind of this, a child comes and you know that he has been abused, it's not optional for you to say I'm not reporting. A teacher who observes something going on, it's not optional. You have to report. So it becomes part of the law,” he said.

results.title: How Hubtel is rethinking AI in Ghana: Own your data, rent the intelligence
results.content: From the trader at Makola checking prices on her phone to the graduate in Kumasi searching for work, one question is getting louder across Ghana. Will artificial intelligence make life better, or will it take away what people already have? Ghana has placed its bet. In 2025 it launched a ten-year national AI strategy, and government has committed $270 million to get the country ready. But for ordinary Ghanaians, the most useful answers may come from a local company that has already tried, stumbled and found a smarter way forward. That company is Hubtel. Head of Engineering, Augustine Adjei, told the national audience during the premiere of the AI & Ghana’s documentary on Joy News, exactly what Ghana’s AI journey looks like from the inside, and why the country does not need to start big to win.

results.title: Minerals Commission defends termination of Northern Ashanti Mines’ licences over $8.38m debt
results.content: The Minerals Commission has defended its decision to terminate the mining leases and prospecting licences of Northern Ashanti Mines Limited, formerly Ower Mines, citing more than US$8.38 million in unpaid fees and alleged breaches of the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703). In a statement issued on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, the Commission said it followed the legally prescribed process after the company failed to settle outstanding Annual Mineral Right (AMR) fees or remedy other breaches identified by the regulator. The company has instituted legal proceedings against the State to challenge the termination, according to the Commission. The Commission said Northern Ashanti Mines acquired a mining lease covering 595 cadastral blocks in January 2010.
